CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Government is the Central Government. 2. Region is Bantul Regency. 3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Bantul Regency as an element of Regional Government administration. 5. Regent is the Regent of Bantul. 6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of Bantul Regency. 7. Woman is a person who is female by sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman. 8. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child still in the womb. 9. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering, whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological, threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life against victims. 10. Violence against women is any action that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life. 11. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, psychologically, sexually, neglect, exploitation, economically, and other violence. 12. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causes death. 13. Psychological Violence is any act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. 14. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. 15. Economic Violence is any act that neglects family members in the form of not providing proper living care or maintenance. 16. Exploitation of Children is any act involving children in activities that may harm their welfare and development or endanger the safety of children with the aim of enabling others to obtain economic, sexual, social, or political benefits, including if it contains restrictions or elimination of opportunities for children to obtain their rights. 17. Sexual harassment is any action with sexual nuances conveyed through physical or non-physical contact that targets sexual body parts or a person's sexuality, including by using whistles, winking, comments or sexually nuanced speech, displaying pornographic materials and sexual desires, pinching or touching body parts, movements or gestures that are sexual in nature resulting in feelings of discomfort, offense, feeling degraded in dignity, and possibly causing health and safety problems. 18. Victim is a Child and Woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the area of Bantul Regency. 19. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children. 20. Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center. 21. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security for women carried out by family members, police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred. 22. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 23. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 24. Women's Empowerment is any effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 25. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has expertise in accompanying victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of violence victims. 26. Spiritual guidance is assistance in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that feelings of calm, security arise, and mental health is achieved. 27. Judicial body is a general court that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice. 28. Prosecution is the action of a public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent District Court in the manner and according to the procedures regulated in the Law with a request to be examined and decided by a judge in a court session. 29. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed them in a civil manner. 30. Institution is an agency/office/body/office within the scope of the Regional Government and/or Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) that provides assistance to victims of violence. 31. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence based in hospitals, and is managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychosocial and legal services. 32.

REGIONAL SECRETARY OF BANTUL REGENCY,
RIYANTONO
REGIONAL GAZETTE OF BANTUL REGENCY YEAR 2013 NUMBER 15
ELUCIDATION
ON
REGIONAL REGULATION OF BANTUL REGENCY
NUMBER 15 YEAR 2013
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
One of the objectives of the establishment of the state is to provide protection to every citizen with a sense of security and comfort, this is expressly stated in the Preamble of the Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia Fourth Paragraph. It is stated that the national objective of the Indonesian nation is to protect all Indonesian people and all Indonesian territory, to advance general welfare, to educate the life of the nation and to participate in implementing world order based on independence, eternal peace and social justice. To achieve this, sustainable development efforts have been carried out which constitute a comprehensive, directed and integrated series of development, including development in promoting gender equality and women's empowerment. This is as affirmed in the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). The implementation of gender equality and women's empowerment has become a priority that is always being improved from year to year, especially since 2000, when Presidential Instruction Number 9 Year 2000 concerning Gender Mainstreaming (PUG) was issued at the urging of the State Minister for Women's Empowerment (Meneg PP) at that time. This Presidential Instruction affirms that all Ministries and non-Ministerial government institutions in the National Government, Provinces, and Regencies/Cities must carry out gender mainstreaming in planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies and programs. This is a manifestation of efforts to fulfill the human rights of every Indonesian citizen, also intended so that gender equality and women's empowerment in Indonesia will increasingly improve. Indonesia as a country that has ratified the International Convention, namely the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW) in the form of Law Number 7 Year 1984 concerning Ratification of the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women, has thereby bound itself to guarantee through legislation, policies, programs and temporary special measures (affirmative action), to realize equality and justice between women and men, as well as the elimination of all forms of discrimination against women, including acts of violence against women and children. It is a breath of fresh air for Indonesian women, when clearly explained in the said Convention which establishes principles and provisions to eliminate disparities, subordination and actions that violate women's rights and harm the position of women in law, family and society. These principles are clearly contained in the substantive articles of the Convention (articles 1-16). Through Law Number 23 Year 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. Human rights inherent in children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation. To fulfill the Right to life, children need food in sufficient quantities, healthy and nutritious, as well as optimal health access. Protection from violence that threatens their safety and health must be provided from an early age. Protection is needed to prevent physical, mental and sexual violence and exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, education that is appropriate to their physical and mental development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents are obliged to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and law enforcement officials who defend the interests of children is needed for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled to defend the best interests of children is needed to realize protection that is legal in nature. Furthermore, it is not uncommon to find cases of women and children who experience problems of physical, psychological, sexual and social violence. For example, women and children victims of assault/abuse, neglect, expulsion and maltreatment by parents or others. For women and children who experience these problems, the government must provide Safe Houses or Integrated Service Centers (PPT) for women and children victims of violence. Safe Houses or PPT are safe places and are friendly to women and children. The PPT is equipped with assistants/counselors from among educators, doctors, psychologists, clerics/religious leaders and is networked with lawyers for women and children as well as RPK Units at the Police. The fate of women and children victims of violence must be given attention by the government. The large number of cases of violence against women and children are often caused by factors that develop in society, such as low economic levels, education, environments in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence like this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights. For the empowerment of victims of violence, local governments can establish Integrated Service Centers and Forums for the Protection of Victims of Violence (FPKK) as centers for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically have the main tasks and functions for empowerment of children and women victims of violence. From the framework above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children.

Article 11
The obligations and responsibilities of the community towards the protection of children and Women Victims of violence are:
a. preventing the occurrence of violence against children and women; b. providing education on a culture of peace and gender equality; c. providing information and/or reporting if acts of violence against children and women occur to law enforcement officials or authorized parties;
d. protecting victims; and
e. providing emergency assistance.

Article 13
(1) In order to provide services and protection to victims of acts of violence, the Regional Government establishes PPT.
(2) PPT as referred to in paragraph (1) has the duties, principal tasks, and functions of providing protection to Children and Women from acts of violence, which consist of fields.
(3) PPT as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be determined by Regent's Decree.
(4) PPT as referred to in paragraph (2) is tasked with providing services and temporary protection in the form of safe houses for victims of violence.
(5) In the event that PPT does not have a safe house (shelter) as referred to in paragraph (3), then victims of violence shall be referred to other institutions.

Article 12
The obligations of the family and/or parents as referred to in Article 6 letter c and letter d, legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of acts of violence and protect children and women as family members.

Article 3
Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Letter a What is meant by the “prevention” aspect is a protection strategy effort through:
a. Primary prevention, all people, families, communities and the state in efforts to increase the ability of knowledge, understanding and ensuring that violence against women and children does not occur, including policy socialization, adequate services, supportive workplace policies, and life skills training for women and children. What is meant by life skills training includes conflict resolution without violence, stress management skills, resource management, effective decision making, effective interpersonal communication, guidance for the psychosocial development of women and children.
b. Secondary prevention, aimed at community groups with high risk in efforts to increase skills, including training and victim services to ensure that violence against women and children does not occur in the next generation. Activities carried out here include conducting home visits for parents who have just had children to conduct self assessment whether they are at risk of committing violence against children in the future.
c. Tertiary prevention, intended to increase parenting abilities that ensure that violence against women and children is not repeated, what is done here is integrated services for women and children who are victims of violence, through counseling, stress management training.
Letter b What is meant by the “service and assistance” aspect is immediate activities and actions carried out by professionals and assistants in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
Letter c What is meant by the “empowerment” aspect is the process of increasing the role of the community to participate in the implementation of protection for women and children victims of acts of violence which aims to obtain access and participation in the process of protection of women and children broadly.

Article 42
(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector in the protection of children and women from acts of violence.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out through: a. employment opportunity information system for women victims of acts of violence;
b. education and training for children and women victims of acts of violence;
c. educational assistance for children and women victims of acts of violence who are vulnerable to dropping out of school; and
d. fostering and increasing economic independence of women victims of acts of violence.
(3) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are set forth in the form of a joint agreement.

CHAPTER X
COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION
Article 46
(1) The community participates in the implementation of protection for victims of acts of violence.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of: a. establishing family partners at the kelurahan/village level by the community; b. establishing Child and Women protection units within community organizations;
c. conducting socialization of the rights of Children and Women independently; d. providing first aid to victims; and
e. reporting to the competent authorities if violence against victims occurs in their environment.
(3) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, social community institutions, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, religious institutions, the private sector, and mass media.

1.9.rationale: The original Indonesian regulation explicitly covers sexual exploitation (a key part of the indicator), so a correct answer should be Yes. In Pasal 1 angka 16, “Eksploitasi Terhadap Anak” is defined as acts involving children to benefit others “ekonomi, seksual, sosial, atau juga politik” (including sexual benefits). In addition, Pasal 1 angka 14 defines “Kekerasan Seksual” to include forced sex “dengan orang lain untuk tujuan komersial” (commercial purposes), which overlaps with sexual exploitation. These points were present in the retrieved English candidates (especially [1.9-3], which includes the sexual-benefit language), but the judge incorrectly claimed there was no explicit sexual exploitation/sexual slavery. The policy does not clearly mention ‘sexual slavery’ as a term, but it does explicitly mention sexual exploitation; the judge’s reasoning was too strict given the indicator wording (‘sexual slavery/exploitation’).

Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear.

Paragraph (2)
a. What is meant by “work network” includes: family partners, dasawisma, and family groups existing in the community. What is meant by “coordination” includes: planning, implementation, and monitoring of violence prevention programs.

Letter a Prevention efforts within the family and/or closest relatives can be carried out by strengthening resilience within the household such as: practicing religious values, managing household time, and communication between family members.

CHAPTER VII
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 44
(1) Regional Government conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of PPT Minimum Service Standards.
(2) Guidance and Supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. coordination;
b. guidance;
c. education and training; and
d. monitoring and evaluation.
(3) Coordination as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a covers aspects related to planning and implementation.
(4) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b covers aspects related to planning, implementation, procedures, funding, quality, control and supervision.
(5) Education and training as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c shall be conducted by SKPD responsible for women's empowerment and child protection.
(6) Monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d shall be conducted periodically.

Paragraph 1
Empowerment of Women Victims of Violence

Article 37
Forms of empowerment for women victims of violence include: a. job training, comprising:
1. skills training;
2. field work practice; and
3. apprenticeship.
b. productive economic enterprises and joint business groups, comprising: 1. entrepreneurial skills training;
2. facilitation of joint business group formation; and
3. business implementation assistance.
c. capital assistance, comprising:
1. work facilities and infrastructure assistance; and
2. working capital assistance facilitation.
From these various efforts, a legal framework will be realized in the implementation of protection for children and women from acts of violence.

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Article 6
Obligations and responsibilities in the implementation of protection for children and women victims of violence are:
a. Regional Government;
b. community;
c. family; and
d. parents.

Article 4
Letter a What is meant by "the right to have one's dignity respected as a human being" is upholding human rights.
Letter b What is meant by "health and psychological recovery from the suffering experienced by the victim" is assistance provided by health experts (doctors) for physical disorders suffered and by psychologists to victims suffering from trauma/other mental problems to restore the victim's mental condition.
Letter c Sufficiently clear.
Letter d What is meant by "obtaining information" is access and information about the whereabouts of complaint centers, PPT, and all matters related to the fulfillment of their rights and involvement in the decision-making process related to assistance and case developments that contain values, meanings, and messages, whether data, facts or explanations that can be seen, heard, and read presented in various packages and formats in accordance with the development of information and communication technology either electronically or non-electronically related to acts of violence.
Letter e What is meant by "confidentiality of identity" is an effort to guarantee certainty for victims that their identity, medical care and legal handling will not be disseminated.
Letter f What is meant by "optimal service" is service that includes medical, medicolegal, existential, psychosocial and legal.
Letter g What is meant by "the right to compensation" includes: economic empowerment, return costs, health insurance, and education or skills.
Letter h What is meant by "continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage" is handling that does not stop at physical and psychological healing, legal assistance to restore civil rights, but until the victim can resume life in society including restoration of good name and citizenship.
Letter i What is meant by "the right to complaint handling" is the availability of a special integrated service unit by officers.
Letter j Sufficiently clear.
Letter k What is meant by "the right to assistance" includes among others: psychologists, psychiatrists, health experts, clergy, advocates, and family members. Meanwhile, legal assistance is assistance provided by persons and/or legal aid institutions to victims at every level of examination and throughout the legal process.
Letter l Sufficiently clear.

Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the prevention and protection of children and women victims of violence. 33. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers from perpetrators in accordance with predetermined standards. 34. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs. 35. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is the standard steps that must be taken in protecting victims starting from complaints/identification, rehabilitation, health, social rehabilitation, legal services up to return and social reintegration of witnesses and/or victims. 36. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree. 37. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, foster care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 38. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations. 39. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Bantul Regency. 40. Gender responsive budget is a budget that provides and accommodates justice and equality for women and men to access and obtain access, as well as benefits from development programs and participate in decision-making processes and have control over resources. 41. Violence Victim Protection Forum hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK is a coordination forum for handling victims of violence against Children and Women whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner.

4.4.rationale: The original Indonesian text clearly includes prevention through education, so the golden label ‘No’ appears incorrect. Pasal 25 ayat (2) huruf c states “menyelenggarakan komunikasi, informasi, dan pendidikan kritis tentang hak-hak anak dan perempuan bagi masyarakat” (organizing communication, information, and critical education about children’s and women’s rights for the community). The Penjelasan Pasal 3 ayat (2) huruf a also describes ‘pencegahan primer’ including increasing knowledge/understanding and ‘pelatihan keterampilan hidup’ (life skills training). These are exactly education/training-based prevention measures. The retrieved candidates contained this material (e.g., [4.4-30], [4.4-65], [4.4-86]), and the judge’s ‘Yes’ rationale aligns with the Indonesian source text.
